A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MARS research work. Their complete main texts, algorithms, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, allowing retained, relocated, revised, and added material to be distinguished.

before.justification: v1 reports original GPT-2 training experiments on OpenWebText, HellaSwag evaluation, timing measurements, and optimizer sensitivity analyses in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 reports original GPT-2 experiments and adds FineWeb-Edu training, broader downstream evaluations, learning-rate scheduler experiments, and CIFAR-10/100 classification results in Section 5 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–4 retain the same scaled gradient correction, momentum updates, clipping choices, and AdamW/Lion/Shampoo instantiations. MARS-approx was already defined in v1; explicitly identifying it as the experimental default in v2 does not introduce a new method.

E1.justification: Beyond retained OpenWebText and HellaSwag experiments, v2 adds FineWeb-Edu 100B pretraining and CIFAR-10/100 image classification. Downstream coverage expands to ARC-E/C, BoolQ, OBQA, PIQA, WinoGrande, MMLU, and SciQ, substantially broadening the represented data and tasks.

E2.justification: The retained main GPT-2 comparisons expand from AdamW and Muon baselines to include Lion, alongside broader evaluation of MARS-Lion. New CIFAR comparisons include Shampoo, and FineWeb-Edu Tables 7–8 add released GPT-2 checkpoints labeled OpenAI-Comm. as reference comparators.

E3.justification: v2 adds constant-learning-rate experiments, WSD schedules with 10k/20k/50k/100k-step budgets, 5-shot evaluation, a 1.5B-parameter GPT-2 configuration, and a 200-epoch, batch-size-128 CIFAR protocol. The core settings for the retained GPT-2 experiments remain unchanged; inconsistent plotted token axes do not establish changed training budgets.

E4.justification: v2 adds scheduler controls and extends exact-versus-approximate analyses to training-loss curves and all three MARS instantiations on CIFAR. The six-schedule gamma table in v1 is replaced by trajectories for seven constant gamma values in Figure 18. The original isolated cosine learning-rate comparison is superseded by broader scheduler studies.

E5.justification: v1 Figure 4 displays error bars for HellaSwag accuracy; the corresponding v2 results in Tables 3–4 provide point estimates without equivalent uncertainty. The meaning of the original bars is unspecified. Both versions retain base seed 5000, without introducing repeated-run counts or significance tests.

E6.justification: Reported GPT-2-large HellaSwag scores change from 44.20%/42.31% for MARS/AdamW in v1 to 44.64%/41.70% in v2 Table 4. Numerous downstream, FineWeb-Edu, scheduler, and CIFAR results are added; Table 9 reports CIFAR-100 accuracy of 77.38% for MARS-AdamW versus 73.70% for AdamW. These are revised or newly reported results, not demonstrated same-setting improvements between versions.

T1.justification: v2 adds formal assumptions, Theorems 4.4 and 4.6 claiming O(log(T)/T^(2/3)) convergence bounds, gamma-dependent correction terms, and extensive proofs in Appendices B–C. Section 3.3 adds a Nesterov-acceleration derivation. v1's short momentum-identity lemma and proof are retained as Lemma C.1 rather than newly introduced.

C1.justification: The introduction adds a central contribution claiming proved convergence faster than Adam/AdamW and tighter bounds through an optimal gamma schedule. v1's principal contributions were the unified framework, its three instantiations, and empirical GPT-2 advantages; those claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations connecting gamma selection to variance bounds and distinguishing noise cancellation from Nesterov lookahead. It interprets scheduler experiments as evidence for continued training and newly describes exact MARS as more fundamental. v1 mainly discussed training efficiency and the approximation's computation-versus-accuracy tradeoff.

D1.justification: v2 adds a MARS implementation link, explicitly identifies the approximate experimental default, names the evaluation harness, and documents learning-rate and weight-decay search ranges. It also supplies FineWeb-Edu holdout information, the GPT-2 XL architecture, and CIFAR hardware and training details. These disclosures do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: Focused additions acknowledge coefficient-scaled SVRG by Yin et al., AdaSPIDER, and further Nesterov and Adam-convergence literature. The central positioning around preconditioned variance reduction remains. Most existing related-work discussion is retained and moved to Appendix A; Adam/AdamW bibliographic updates concern the same works.

P1.justification: The document is reorganized around a new theory section before experiments. Related work moves from Section 5 to Appendix A, existing experimental analyses move into Appendix D, and the appendices gain a contents page and a substantially reorganized proof structure. Contributions and experimental discussion expand, although much original method prose remains.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the HellaSwag bar chart with multi-benchmark tables, expands optimizer series in retained plots, relocates small/medium GPT-2 figures, adds scheduler and vision panels, and consolidates hyperparameter tables. Some revised training-token axes span 0–5000 billion while paired validation axes span 0–50 billion, as in Figure 1.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves empirical breadth, diagnostic controls, and reproducibility disclosures. However, its new central convergence claims have an unresolved method–proof mismatch: Algorithm 1 clips the gradient estimator, whereas Appendix C.4 derives Lemma B.2 using an unclipped recursion without establishing that clipping is inactive. Removed HellaSwag error bars and inconsistent token axes also weaken reporting. These substantial gains and reliability concerns prevent a confident net quality judgment.
